sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Livingston County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Deeds for Livingston County property go to the Register of Deeds in the historical courthouse at 200 E Grand River Ave in Howell, the county seat. The office phone is (517) 546-0270, and counter hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed on county holidays.

Most documents never reach the counter. Title companies and attorneys send them electronically through four certified vendors: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A few instruments cannot go that way, including deeds that come with valuation affidavits, plats, and master deeds with large drawings. Those must be brought in or mailed on paper.

Livingston County sits in southeast Michigan along I-96, US 23 and M-59, with 585 square miles of area and a 2020 census population of 193,866. About 86 percent of its occupied homes are owner-occupied, so deeds move through this office at a steady pace. The Census Bureau counted Brighton, Howell and nearby South Lyon as one contiguous urbanized area, and employers such as Tribar, PepsiCo and Citizens Insurance anchor the local economy. Sellers outside those towns, in the rural townships, record at the same counter. The county is laid out in 16 townships of 36 one-mile sections each, which is why legal descriptions on a Livingston deed read as a section number plus a starting corner.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Livingston County?
sections.html:
The flat recording fee is $30.00. Of that, $4 goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund. A document that assigns or discharges more than one liber and page, or document number, adds $3 for each reference after the first.

Livingston County Register of Deeds fee schedule from the county FAQ
ServiceFee
Recording a document$30.00 flat
Each extra liber and page cross-reference$3.00
Tax certification, first 25 parcel numbers$5.00, then $0.20 per added number
Fixture filing$30 per document
Copy of a recorded page$1.00 ($2.00 for plat or condo drawings)
Certifying a copy$5.00, all pages must be bought
Tract index use, unless it is your own property$10 per hour

Recording fees and transfer tax cannot be billed to a charge account. They are paid by cash, check or credit card, and a card adds a service fee in proportion to the transaction.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a Livingston County sale?
sections.html:
When a deed shows a sale amount, the office collects transfer tax at the time of recording which the county describes as .086 of the amount, meaning $8.60 per $1,000. Of that, $1.10 per $1,000 goes to the county and $7.50 per $1,000 to the state, and the grantor generally pays it. The price is rounded up to the next $500 first, so a $100,000.01 sale is taxed as $100,500.

On a $300,000 sale the combined tax comes to $2,580 at $8.60 per $1,000. A deed covering land in more than one county must split the price by county on its face.

Exemptions exist, and a deed can be exempt from the state portion alone or from both, never from the county portion alone. The exemption cited must match the facts on the page. Common errors the office lists:

  • Using a parent-to-child or grandparent-to-child exemption when a trust is the grantor, since an individual must sign as grantor.
  • Assuming a church is automatically exempt.
  • Assuming a sheriff's deed escapes county tax. It is always exempt from the state portion, but exempt from the county portion only when the mortgage is federally backed.
  • Citing the under-$100 exemption while the deed shows a $5,000 price.

sections.h2: What is a tax certification and when is it required?
sections.html:
A tax certification is a Treasurer's sticker showing that taxes are paid up and that the legal description matches the township tax roll. It is part of what makes a warranty deed a warranty deed. The county requires it before recording warranty deeds, any deed with "warrant" in the conveyance line, land contracts, assignments of land contract (except those given as collateral), master deeds, and master deed amendments that add property to a condominium.

Mailing the document? Include the $5.00 and the office obtains the certification. E-recording a document that needs one means submitting the package through the document router, so it reaches both departments. The county treasurer's page lists tax clearance of deeds among that office's duties, which is why a seller with unpaid taxes finds out at this stage if not earlier.

sections.h2: How do copies, searches and corrections work in Livingston County?
sections.html:
Searching the index by name is free online. Viewing a page costs $1 plus a convenience fee that covers card processing, and a link arrives immediately. Certified copies, death certificates, tax liens, condo master deeds and documents over 75 pages are mailed after purchase. Records are imaged and indexed back to November 7, 1980 (liber 1000), with earlier books imaged or kept in hard copy.

  • You cannot change a signed, notarized or recorded deed. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed signed by the current owners.
  • When a joint tenant or spouse dies, recording the death certificate shows the survivor as sole owner without a new deed.
  • An enhanced life estate (ladybird) deed becomes proof of ownership once both death certificates are recorded.
  • Paying off a mortgage produces a discharge, not a new deed.
  • A rejected document comes back with a letter listing the reasons, and it can be corrected and resubmitted.

For hard copy submissions by mail or in person, include a self-addressed stamped envelope or $3 in postage. Supplying an email address gets you the recorded copy back free, usually the day it is recorded.

sections.h2: What should a Livingston County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the title company to pull the recorded chain: the vesting deed, any recorded death certificate, mortgage discharges, and liens. The Register of Deeds says it cannot verify ownership, since unrecorded land contracts or deeds can affect it, and its staff do not run title searches or give a guarantee. Title companies do that work and can also check probate court records the recorder lacks.

The county equalization office notes that the buyer files a property transfer affidavit with the local assessor within 45 days, with a fine of $5 a day up to $200 for failing to do so, and the taxable value of the home is uncapped the following year. A seller who knows the taxes will jump for the buyer can say so up front, because it affects what the buyer can afford.

Homes with back taxes, estate paperwork or repair needs are the usual reason owners ask for a cash sale. The recording steps do not change with the buyer type.

faqs.q: How much does the Livingston County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The flat fee is $30.00 per document, including $4 for the state survey and remonumentation fund. Extra cross-references cost $3 each, and transfer tax is separate.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax in Livingston County?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller, generally pays. The county collects it at recording at $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, after rounding the price up to the next $500.

faqs.q: Can I record a photocopy of a deed?
faqs.a: No. Only documents with original signatures can be recorded, and even electronic services must scan originals. Court orders, death certificates and surveys must be certified versions.

faqs.q: How can I add my child's name to my Livingston County deed?
faqs.a: You need a new deed signed by the current owners that conveys the property to everyone who should be on title. A recorded deed cannot be edited. Use a title company or attorney to draft it.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds search titles?
faqs.a: No. The office does not do title searches or furnish abstracts and cannot guarantee results. Title companies perform and insure searches, while the office teaches the public how to use its index.
